notes: Electric-type parts from the LG service manual 3828EL3005A (printed Apr. 2004), which is shared by the DLE3777W, its gas twin the DLG3788W and the DLE5977/DLG5988 models. Newer units may differ.

gaps: The model table rates a 250 W (4.5 A) motor and a 5400 W (22.5 A) heater in cells that sit across the DLE5977/DLG5988 columns; not tied to the DLE3777W, so left out.

Power supply: the table's 120V / 240V 60Hz (26A) cell is not tied to the DLE3777W, and 'AC 240V (ELECTRIC TYPE)' is a remark on the heater row, so no supply claim is made (the researcher's wire_heavy claim dropped).
Heater test (Test 6): the terminal labels are missing from the text, so the three ranges can't be paired to heater terminals.
Thermistor table (Test 2): the 130 F (2.9 kΩ) and 140 F (3.0 kΩ) rows as printed do not fall steadily; only the end points (50 F and 160 F) are given.
The thermal cut-off row also has an 'Auto reset -31 F (-35 C)' line that can't be paired with a part, so it is left out.
Test 3 wire-pair readings are taken at the control connectors, not across the motor windings; no motor winding values are claimed.
No part numbers claimed: the display PWB numbers on page 18 (6871EC1115A to D) and the parts list pages have columns the ManualsLib text separates; no legible part numbers on page 41.
No blower wheel, drum roller, timer, thermal fuse rating or belt part number on the pages read.
method: LG DLE3777W service manual 3828EL3005A (ManualsLib, 41 pages, electric and gas dryer) read through the ManualsLib viewer: cover, then viewer pages 5, 14, 18, 22, 23, 26 and 41.
Page 5 is the model table. Page 14 is component testing. Page 22 is the thermistor test. Page 23 is the motor test. Page 26 is the electric heater test. Page 18 and page 41 are not used for claims.

The ManualsLib text separates table columns, so the model table, thermal cut-off, hi-limit and outlet thermostat rows and the thermistor table were lined up against a text-layer PDF copy of the same manual hosted by a parts retailer (read only for column alignment, not cited).
No bot check, login wall or paywall on any ManualsLib page read.
PartSelect and Sears PartsDirect pages refused the researcher and are not cited.

comps.spec: Electric-type heater. Test 6 (heater switch test, electric type) checks it across three terminal pairs against 18-22 Ω, 18-22 Ω and 9-11 Ω.
Thermal cut-off, top marking N130, opens at 266 ±12 °F (130 ±7 °C); the page lists it as a safety part for the heater case, electric type.
Hi-limit thermostat, auto reset: opens at 257 ±9 °F (125 ±5 °C) and closes at 221 ±9 °F (105 ±5 °C); listed for the heater case, electric type.
Outlet thermostat, auto reset, top marking N85: opens at 185 ±9 °F (85 ±5 °C) and closes at 149 ±9 °F (65 ±5 °C). Listed for the blower housing, electric type.

Temperature thermistor (the model table lists 'Termistor' for the DLE3777W/DLG3788W column). Test 2 checks it at the controller's 6-pin connector on the blue and red wires against a table that runs from 18.0 kΩ at 50 °F to 2.2 kΩ at 160 °F.
Electrode moisture sensor, the 'Electrode sensor' entry in the model table.

Drive motor. Test 3 (drum will not rotate, no fan, no heater) checks for under 3 Ω across white-brown, white-yellow and yellow-brown wire pairs at the control connectors, then sends you to the manual's motor diagram and check page.
Idler assembly and motor pulley, named in the motor test: check the idler assembly, and the drum belt can cut off or come off the motor pulley.
Idler switch attached to the motor bracket, with a lever the drum belt operates. Test 3 checks for under 1 Ω across its terminals and replaces it if not.
Door switch with a knob and COM, NC and NO terminals (1-3 and 1-2). It is read with the knob open and with it pushed, and the pushed state is the reverse of the open one.
